text:
kevin: thinking out loud — we should try a "soft eviction" mode that marks entries as soft-evicted and starts a short lease/handshake instead of hard drop. avoids thundering reads when multiple tenants share a slab

ashley: sounds useful. what's the exact semantics of "soft-evicted"? do we still serve stale values for X ms?

kevin: idea: on soft-evict we set state=SOFT_EVICT + expiry_ts, keep value in slab for grace period (default 200ms). reads hit: if within grace -> serve + async refresh; if expired -> block+fetch. goal: keep p99 down during transient churn

liam: main risk is correctness for prefix caching: model A might read prefix state produced by model B if we let stale get served. that could break deterministic evals.

ashley: agree, for cross-tenant/model correctness we need a version/gen tag on the prefix entries. if entry.gen != expected_gen -> treat as miss (no silent staleness)

kevin: exactly. attach small integer generation+origin tag. cheap: 8 bytes per entry. tradeoff: storage overhead vs fewer correctness incidents.

sara: how do leases interact with shard handoffs? we already saw races when handoff+evict coincide.

kevin: plan: lease token tied to shard epoch. when shard moves, epoch++ and any lease with old epoch is invalid. soft-evict will include epoch awareness. also add a short grace where new owner can request a transfer instead of immediate reclaim

liam: still worried about read-after-write within same request path (client writes prefix, then immediate read). we must ensure read-after-write is linearizable for pinned prefixes.

kevin: pinned prefixes = strong semantics: always require write to confirm to owning node before returning. soft-evict only applies to non-pinned prefixes. we need clear API tags: pin=true vs pin=false

ashley: can we express config as something like:

```yaml
cache:
  soft_eviction:
    enabled: true
    grace_ms: 200
    gen_tag: true
  leases:
    default_ttl_ms: 500
    heartbeat_ms: 150
    shard_epoch_check: true
  policies:
    tenant_priority:
      enabled: true
      weights: { "enterprise": 100, "freemium": 10 }
```

liam: tenant_priority weights are useful but we need to simulate fairness: high-weight tenants could starve low ones if eviction hysteresis too long. add min-reserve per-tenant

kevin: good call. reserve + soft-evict hysteresis + eviction score = composite. eviction_score = (age_factor * age) + (size_factor * size) - (priority_weight) + penalty_if_pinned

sara: how do we detect stale reads in production to validate gen-tag idea? metrics?

kevin: add counters: stale_read_count, stale_read_rate, forced_miss_after_soft_evict, lease_renew_failures. also sample stack traces for occurrences to see common codepaths.

runtime-bot: note: created follow-up issue INF-6421 for metrics + sim harness (assigned to kevin) :white_check_mark:

liam: any perf cost of gen_tag compare on hot path? CPU overhead negligible but increases cache footprint; need microbench.

kevin: agreed — benchmark plan: 1) mem overhead (MB) for gen tag at 50M entries; 2) p99 read latency with and without soft-evict; 3) stale read incidence under high churn.

ashley: test harness should also run multi-model sharing scenario where same prefix keys are used by different models to validate origin tag correctness

kevin: next steps:
- kevin: prototype soft-evict state + gen tag in runtime (spike, 2d)
- liam: add microbench and allocate perf slot (1d)
- ashley: write integration test matrix incl. read-after-write, multi-model prefix, shard-handoff race (2d)
- sara: define metrics/dashboards and alerts (1d)

sara: can we also add an emergency flag to force immediate hard-evict when memory critical? e.g., oom_pressure_override = true

kevin: yes — emergency_hard_evict kicks in if free_memory < threshold or gc pressure high. soft-evict only used under normal ops

liam: FYI we should doc the API changes for pin/gen/priority in the public SDKs so client teams don't accidentally rely on stale-serving behavior

kevin: i'll draft a short RFC after prototype. tagging @sara @liam @ashley for review. anyone else to pull in?

ashley: ping @platform for observability hooks after we have metrics names

runtime-bot: scheduled: RFC draft review meeting on 2026-04-02 16:00 UTC (calendar invite sent)

kevin: thanks everyone — will post spike PR in eng-runtime when ready, and link the issue INF-6421. :rocket:
